primary_singles.learning: Toluca cleared the frozen Kelly gate despite a modest raw edge because 63.1% model probability exceeded the 60.2% break-even threshold enough to justify the minimum 10 MXN stake. Record as a normal value hit, not proof that champions or favorites should be chased.

The model priced the Over above the 50% break-even point and it won in a five-goal match. Because researcher outcome exposure preceded the final freeze, this is usable for accounting and diagnostics only, never as evidence to promote total-goals logic.

selected_single_metrics.note: Raw beat calibration shadow on the two selected J2 singles because both higher raw probabilities won. n=2 is trivial and J2 is NO-PROMOTION.

apertura_selected_singles_diagnostic_thr.note: Across J1+J2 selected singles the calibration shadow still leads cumulatively, but both jornadas are researcher-outcome-exposed and therefore diagnostic only.

learning: The strongest operational signal in J2 is selectivity: only 25 of the 100 MXN maximum risk budget qualified. A ceiling is not a spending target.
America ML was rejected despite a 74.8% raw win probability because the frozen 1.35 price implied 74.1% break-even and Kelly score was only 0.0294, below the 0.05 gate.

San Luis-Monterrey draw had positive model EV at 4.50 but missed the Kelly gate narrowly at 0.04946. The rule rejected it mechanically; do not lower the threshold because the eventual result is known.
No two-leg parlay qualified because no window contained two approved primary singles. This is intended behavior, not a missing bet.
Raw calibration metrics beat the shadow on J2's two wins, while the cumulative J1+J2 diagnostic still favors the shadow. Preserve both; do not refit or promote.
J2 cannot provide clean context-learning evidence because outcome exposure occurred before final freeze. Context should not be retrospectively graded to fit what happened.
